headline: Nasdaq falls over 1% as investors rotate out of semiconductor stocks
summary: The Nasdaq index opened more than 1% lower as investors rotated out of chip stocks following the U.S. midterm elections. The shift reflects a broader market adjustment in the wake of the political results.
why: The semiconductor sector is a high-growth area of the tech market, often sensitive to changes in trade policy and government regulation.

impacts.name: Semiconductors
impacts.why: Broad selling pressure in the chip sector following political shifts.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Market participants are reallocating capital away from semiconductor stocks in response to the U.S. midterm election outcomes.
